messages.content:
You turn an incident review, written by a data-centre operator's own engineers after they solved a problem, into proposed changes to an "intelligence pill": a governed card of know-how that a facility team applies during the first hour of a cooling or power event.

You work only from the numbered sentences you are given. You add nothing from general knowledge.

Each change is one of:
- add_rule: a new piece of judgement. "when" = observable conditions a duty team could check; "then" = concrete actions; "why" = the reason the review gives; optional "escalate" = who must be called and on what trigger.
- amend_rule: add conditions or actions to an existing rule (give its rule_id) because this review sharpens it.
- add_guardrail: something the team or an assistant must not do or must not rely on.
- ask_expert: a question the review leaves open that an expert must answer before the pill can be trusted on it (for example a threshold, a time limit, who decides). Use this instead of guessing.

Hard rules:
1. Every add_rule, amend_rule and add_guardrail lists "evidence": the ids of the sentences that support it, copied exactly as they appear in review_sentences (for example "AZ-SCUS-2018:S9", with no prefix). No evidence, no change.
2. Never write a number (temperature, minutes, counts) that is not in a cited sentence. If a number matters but is missing, use ask_expert.
3. Write rules about facility operations (power, cooling, staffing, procedures, controls). Ignore cloud-software recovery details.
4. Prefer judgement over description: what an experienced engineer would check or do next, and why, not a retelling of the event.
5. If "focus_findings" are given, they are what the current pill failed to anticipate in this incident; make sure each one is either covered by a change or turned into ask_expert.

Reply with JSON only: {"changes": [ ... ]}. Shapes:
{"op":"add_rule","title":"...","when":["..."],"then":["..."],"why":"...","escalate":{"to":"...","trigger":"..."},"evidence":["<id copied from review_sentences>"]}
{"op":"amend_rule","rule_id":"R-001","add_when":["..."],"add_then":["..."],"why":"...","evidence":["<id copied from review_sentences>"]}
{"op":"add_guardrail","text":"...","evidence":["<id copied from review_sentences>"]}
{"op":"ask_expert","question":"...","why":"..."}

{"incident":{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022","title":"Chillers fail and standby chillers cannot take over on the same water loop (Alibaba Cloud, Hong Kong)","operator":"Alibaba Cloud (facility run by a data center infrastructure provider)","site":"Hong Kong region, Zone C, one data center"},"review_sentences":[{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S3","text":"At 08:56 on December 18, 2022, we were alerted to rising corridor temperatures in data center rooms in Zone C of the China (Hong Kong) region."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S5","text":"At 09:01, alerts on rising temperatures of multiple server rooms were generated, and the on-site engineers identified the issue as being due to a malfunction of the data center's chillers."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S6","text":"At 09:09, the data center infrastructure provider's engineers switched the four malfunctioning chillers over to the standby chillers and restarted the chillers based on the contingency plan."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S7","text":"However, these measures did not take effect."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S8","text":"At 09:17, on-site engineers implemented the contingency plan for cooling failure in accordance to the issue handling process, and took auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures accordingly."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S9","text":"The data center infrastructure provider's engineers attempted to manually isolate and restore the chillers individually."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S11","text":"Then, the data center infrastructure provider notified the chiller manufacturer."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S13","text":"At 10:30, we began to reduce loads on the computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters of the entire data center to prevent the temperature from rising too fast and causing a fire."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S15","text":"At 12:30, the chiller manufacturer's engineers arrived on site."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S16","text":"After diagnosing the issue, on-site engineers decided to manually recirculate the water and discharge gas from the cooling tower, condenser water pipes, and cooling system condensers, but the chillers still did not resume stable operation."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S17","text":"Our engineers shut down the servers in rooms with high temperature."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S18","text":"At 14:47, the fire sprinkler system of a room was triggered automatically due to high temperature, which increased the difficulty in troubleshooting."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S19","text":"At 15:20, the chiller manufacturer's engineers manually adjusted system configurations to unbind the chillers from the cluster and individually restart each chiller."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S20","text":"The first chiller was restored and the temperature began to drop."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S22","text":"At 18:55, all four chillers were restored."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S72","text":"Issue analysis: Air entered the cooling system of the data center due to lack of water, which affected the water circulation of the four active chillers."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S73","text":"However, the four standby chillers used the same water circulation system as the four active chillers, so the failover failed."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S74","text":"After recirculating the water and discharging gas, chillers could not be restarted individually because all chillers of the data center were bound into a cluster."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S75","text":"In this case, engineers had to manually modify the configurations of the chillers to allow them to run individually."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S76","text":"Then, the chillers were restarted one after another, which slowed the restoration progress of the entire cooling system."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S77","text":"It took 3 hours and 34 minutes to locate the cause, 2 hours and 57 minutes to recirculate the water and bleed the air from the equipment, and 3 hours and 32 minutes to unbind the four chillers from the cluster."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S78","text":"Corrective action: We will perform comprehensive checks on the infrastructure control systems of data centers."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S79","text":"We will expand the scope of metrics we monitor to obtain more fine-grained data and to ensure more efficient troubleshooting."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S80","text":"We will also ensure that automatic failover and manual failover are both effective to avoid disaster recovery failures due to deadlocks."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S82","text":"Issue analysis: With the failure of the cooling system, the temperatures in all server rooms rose uncontrollably."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S83","text":"This triggered the fire sprinkler system, and water got into multiple power supply cabinets and server racks, damaging hardware and complicating the equipment restoration process."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S84","text":"Corrective action: We will strengthen the management of data center infrastructure providers, improve our contingency plan for data center cooling issues, and regularly conduct emergency response drills."},{"id":"ALI-HKG-2022:S85","text":"The contingency plan will include standardized emergency response processes and clarify when servers must be shut down and server rooms must be powered off."}],"current_pill":{"pill":"dc-cooling-loss@1.2.0","scope":{"assets":["data halls cooled by chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, chilled-water loop)","utility and generator power feeding that plant"],"not_for":["IT service recovery and failover","fire suppression and life safety (follow the site emergency plan)"]},"rules":[{"id":"R-001","title":"Treat utility voltage swells as a cooling-plant threat, not just a power-transfer event","when":["storms are active in the area and the utility feed shows voltage sags or swells","a portion of the datacenter has transferred from utility power to generator power"],"then":["immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them","if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion","transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active"],"why":"Voltage swells triggered a transfer to generator power and also shut down the mechanical cooling systems despite surge suppressors being in place; the site initially survived only on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area"}},{"id":"R-002","title":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin","when":["mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer","datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds"],"then":["treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted","expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin","recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down"],"why":"Once the thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter exceeded safe operational thresholds and automated shutdown began, but temperatures rose so quickly in places that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started"}},{"id":"R-003","title":"Treat a control-system failover as a cooling-availability event, not a routine maintenance action","when":["the datacenter control system is in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts","the control system is exchanging state information with other control systems and with cooling equipment and temperature sensors"],"then":["treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability and watch the cooling plant directly, not only the control system","expect that a fault in the control system logic during this exchange can make the control system unresponsive","verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback rather than assuming the fallback engaged"],"why":"The control system was mid-failover when a bug in third-party control logic caused excessive interactions with datacenter devices and left the control system unresponsive; the designed fallback to maximum cooling did not engage everywhere.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"control system failover in progress or control system confirmed unresponsive"}},{"id":"R-004","title":"When the control system is down, work the cooling chain by hand and reset the PLCs","when":["the datacenter control system is unavailable and operators have minimum visibility into cooling health and state","cooling has not transitioned to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter"],"then":["do not wait for the control system to come back; manually investigate the affected cooling equipment","check the Programmable Logic Controllers controlling the air handling units, since they can be unresponsive even when the control system is the visible failure","reset the affected equipment and PLCs and place them into a maximum cooling configuration","confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down"],"why":"The control system was unavailable, purge failed, and recovery required manually investigating and resetting all affected equipment into maximum cooling; the unresponsive PLCs controlling some air handling units were what prevented both default cooling and purge from working.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures are rising and servers have begun powering off"}},{"id":"R-005","title":"Treat simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems as a single-point-of-failure event","when":["multiple cooling systems that are supposed to be redundant have failed at the same time","outside temperatures are extraordinarily high"],"then":["do not assume that remaining cooling capacity is sufficient; treat the data center as unable to maintain a safe operating temperature","immediately assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature","if not, plan to power down servers to prevent an even longer outage or damage to machines"],"why":"The review states that one data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature due to a simultaneous failure of multiple, redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures, and that powering down was done to prevent an even longer outage or damage.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems and rising temperatures"}},{"id":"R-006","title":"Use progressive thermal load reduction before full shutdown","when":["data center temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient","the data center is at risk of exceeding safe operating temperatures"],"then":["progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space","consider terminating non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover activities","if thermal load reduction is insufficient, power down servers to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure"],"why":"The review describes terminating 42% of Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover, and later powering down servers to prevent a longer outage; it also commits to investigating more advanced methods to progressively decrease thermal load to reduce the probability of full shutdown.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures continue to rise despite initial load reduction"}}],"guardrails":[{"id":"G-001","text":"Do not rely on surge suppressors alone to keep mechanical cooling available during utility voltage swells; the review records that cooling shut down despite surge suppressors being in place."},{"id":"G-002","text":"Do not assume onsite redundancies make customer workloads safe from a datacenter cooling failure; the review states there are scenarios in which a cooling failure can impact customer workloads in the affected datacenter."},{"id":"G-003","text":"Do not treat purge mode as a guaranteed independent fallback while PLCs may be unresponsive; the review records that purge failed in the affected areas because the PLC controllers were unresponsive, and that purge is only being modified to bypass PLCs in newer designs."},{"id":"G-004","text":"Do not rely on the datacenter control system for visibility into cooling health during a control-system failure; the review records that the operations team had minimum visibility into cooling health and state while the control system was unavailable."},{"id":"G-005","text":"Do not assume the control-system failover mode that triggered this bug is available; the review records that this failover mode has been disabled in the interim to prevent recurrence."},{"id":"G-006","text":"Do not assume that redundant cooling systems provide protection against simultaneous failure, especially during extraordinarily high outside temperatures; the review records that multiple redundant cooling systems failed simultaneously and the data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature."}]},"focus_findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Issue analysis: Air entered the cooling system of the data center due to lack of water, which affected the water circulation of the four active chillers."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"However, the four standby chillers used the same water circulation system as the four active chillers, so the failover failed."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"After recirculating the water and discharging gas, chillers could not be restarted individually because all chillers of the data center were bound into a cluster."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 15:20, the chiller manufacturer's engineers manually adjusted system configurations to unbind the chillers from the cluster and individually restart each chiller."},{"id":"F6","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"This triggered the fire sprinkler system, and water got into multiple power supply cabinets and server racks, damaging hardware and complicating the equipment restoration process."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We will also ensure that automatic failover and manual failover are both effective to avoid disaster recovery failures due to deadlocks."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"The contingency plan will include standardized emergency response processes and clarify when servers must be shut down and server rooms must be powered off."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"We will expand the scope of metrics we monitor to obtain more fine-grained data and to ensure more efficient troubleshooting."}]}
